composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-114b, "BILGE / WATER VALVE SYSTEM") wires five motor-operated fresh water valves via terminal strip T/S B (terminals 51-75), relays Re7-Re11, and XA60/XA41 cross-references. Despite the sheet title referencing "BILGE", the loads named on the sheet are all FRESH WATER valves (FRESH WATER VALVE, FRESH WATER PORT BUNKER, FRESH WATER STBD BUNKER, FRESH WATER PORT SUCTION, FRESH WATER STBD SUCTION), fed from a breaker labelled "WATER TRANSFER VALVES Q14 10A". The engineer-confirmed mapping ties "WATER TRANSFER VALVES" to node 510-water-transfer-valves, and this is corroborated by an established fact that Q14 10A is the electrical supply for 520-bilge-valves per the +24V DC Distribution sheet — however, that established fact's panel/rating context (EMERGENCY POWER SUPPLY) differs from this sheet's load labelling by name (all valves here are named FRESH WATER, not BILGE). Per engineer-confirmed vocabulary, "WATER TRANSFER VALVES" -> 510-water-transfer-valves, so all five valve loads are composed onto that node. The T/S B terminal strip, relay bank and XA60/XA41 cross-connect structure are infrastructure of that node's control loop (not a separate distribution unit).

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Load name 'FRESH WATER VALVE' matches the engineer-confirmed mapping WATER TRANSFER VALVES -> 510-water-transfer-valves; fed from the WATER TRANSFER VALVES Q14 10A breaker via T/S B terminal 14 and relay Re7.

functions.label: Open/close the main fresh water valve on remote command
functions.what_it_does: A motor-operated valve (M) opens or closes the fresh water line under remote OPEN/CLOSE command, switched through relay Re7. The relay's coil is energised by a NEGATIVE supplied from XA41 terminal 10 (settled by engineer: XA41 terminals are the CONTROL, supplying relay coil negative); the relay in turn supplies POSITIVE to the valve motor. XA60 terminals 02/04 are SIGNAL taps to the Onyx monitoring system, not control commands (engineer-settled).

flow_scenarios.path: +24V Service Bat. -> F6 300A fuse -> Q14 10A breaker (WATER TRANSFER VALVES) -> T/S B terminal 14 -> Re7 contact common
XA41 terminal 10 -> terminal 55 -> Re7 coil negative; Re7 energised -> supplies positive to valve motor pins via terminals 53(pin3)/54(pin2) -> FRESH WATER VALVE motor opens/closes
OPEN/CLOSE contact pair (terminals 51/52) <-> XA60 pins 02/04 -> signal to Onyx monitoring (status/command direction to Onyx system itself, cross-reference only)

infrastructure.system_name: T/S B terminal strip and bus feed (WATER TRANSFER VALVES supply chain)
facts: Fed from +24V SERVICE BAT. through fuse F6 (300A) and breaker Q14 (10A, labelled WATER TRANSFER VALVES) into the vertical bus feeding T/S B terminals 14/15/16/17/18 in daisy-chain (14->15->16->17->18)
This is a control/relay wiring diagram (relay_terminal_wiring sub-type), not a fluid P&ID; distribution schedule / one-line topology does not apply here

Consistent with established fact that Q14 10A / WATER TRANSFER VALVES is the breaker feed shown on the +24V DC Distribution sheet; that established fact labels it under 520-bilge-valves but the engineer-confirmed vocabulary map assigns the load name WATER TRANSFER VALVES to 510-water-transfer-valves — recorded as an identity note, not re-derived

uncertainties: The sheet's own title is 'BILGE / WATER VALVE SYSTEM' but every named load on this sheet is a FRESH WATER valve (FRESH WATER VALVE, PORT/STBD BUNKER, PORT/STBD SUCTION) — none are named as bilge valves. The engineer-confirmed vocabulary maps 'WATER TRANSFER VALVES' (the breaker label) to 510-water-transfer-valves, which is followed here; however an established fact on a DIFFERENT sheet (+24V DC Distribution) attaches the same Q14/10A breaker to node 520-bilge-valves. This is a naming/identity conflict between two sheets sharing the same breaker label but different equipment — needs engineer confirmation on whether 510-water-transfer-valves and 520-bilge-valves are being fed by the same Q14, or whether there are two distinct Q14 breakers (one per panel) not distinguished across sheets.
